### God Will Reward
Author: Charles R. Swindoll
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/todays-insight-chuck-swindoll/todays-insight-august-12-2020.html
Passage: Job 23:10
Points:
- Job expresses confident faith that God is aware of his situation and is the one testing him.
- Spiritual growth cannot bypass suffering, just as refining pure gold requires intense heat.
- Every believer faces different trials suited to their life and spiritual maturity.
- Hardships serve a divine purpose to purify, humble, and reshape our character.
- God remembers our trials and will ultimately reward faithfulness, whether in this life or in eternity.

### Coming Through as Pure Gold
Author: Adrian Rogers
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/loveworthfinding/love-worth-finding-january-10-2012.html
Passage: Job 23:10
Points:
- A craftsman heats metal over fire until impurities are removed and his reflection appears.
- God uses trials to refine believers until His own character is reproduced in them.
- Even when the heat of testing feels intense, God remains in total control of the fire.
- Whatever painful losses God permits in a trial are things we do not truly need.

### Exit Numbers
Author: Marybeth Whalen
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/encouragement/encouragement-for-today-oct-3-2008-11582526.html
Passage: Job 23:10
Points:
- Navigating a long journey becomes manageable when you focus on clear guide markers.
- God gives spiritual guidance through Scripture, the Holy Spirit, and promised ways out of temptation.
- Distractions, pace of life, and spiritual attacks attempt to divert believers from God's path.
- When feeling stalled or overwhelmed, believers can refocus on God's guidance and seek encouragement from others.

### Devotional: Job 23
Author: D. A. Carson
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/devotionals/read-the-bible/exodus-6-luke-9-job-23-1-corinthians-10/
Passage: Job 23:1-17
Points:
- Job turns from debating his companions to voicing his struggle with God's apparent absence and silence.
- Job maintains firm confidence that God knows where he is and recognizes his moral integrity.
- Job's deepest dread is not God's destructive power, but the terror of God remaining inaccessible.
- In seasons where God seems hidden, believers must remember the larger story and its final resolution.
